# readsb

**Efficient Mode S and ADS-B decoder — the maintained dump1090 successor**

- **Version recorded:** 3.14.1630
- **Categories:** `aircraft`
- **Upstream:** <https://github.com/adsbfi/readsb>
- **Supersedes:** `dump1090`

## What it does

Decodes Mode S, ADS-B and TIS-B from an SDR and serves the results: a built-in web map, Beast and raw output for other software, SBS format for older tools, and JSON for anything else. It drives RTL-SDR, bladeRF and dedicated Mode S receivers, and it is written to be efficient enough to run continuously on a Raspberry Pi.

## Why you would want it

ADS-B is the most immediately rewarding thing to do with a cheap dongle: aircraft appear on a map within a minute of getting the antenna outside. readsb is the maintained line of that software -- dump1090 forked several times and this is the fork that is still developed -- and its decoder recovers more messages from weak signals than the original.

## Before it will work

An SDR that reaches 1090 MHz, and an antenna for it. Antenna matters more than the receiver: a proper quarter-wave or collinear outside will multiply the range over a stub on a desk, and 1090 MHz is line of sight, so height is everything.

## Install and launch

- **Installed with the profile:** [`listening`](../profiles/listening.md).
- **Install:** `hammunition install readsb --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Its package ships its own commands and application-menu entry; a unit that ships none gets a generated terminal entry (**D-050**). `hammunition status` lists what is installed.
- **The install needs the network to:** your distribution's package archive.

## Offline use

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

## How it installs

- apt: `readsb`
  - Present on Debian 13, Ubuntu 26.04, Kali and Parrot; absent on Linux Mint 22.3 (measured 2026-08-28). Debian 13 does NOT carry `dump1090-mutability`, which Ubuntu and Mint do -- so on Debian the older name is not a fallback and this is the ADS-B decoder available.

## Known problems

It wants exclusive use of the dongle; anything else holding the device means it will not start. Feeding aggregator networks is a choice with a privacy dimension -- you are publishing what your receiver hears, and where it is, to a third party -- and it is off unless configured. The web map binds locally by default; exposing it publishes your receiver's location.
